description: Figure 4 is a grouped bar chart that compares the popularity of entities in correctly and incorrectly answered samples across three domains: Movies, Songs, and Basketball. The vertical axis, labeled “Popularity,” ranges from 0 to 220, with tick marks at intervals of 20. The horizontal axis displays the three domains, each containing a cluster of six bars representing different model-entity combinations. The legend identifies six categories: Llama3 (solid blue), Qwen2 (solid red), ChatGPT (solid yellow), Acc=0 & GT Ans (blue with diagonal stripes), Acc=0 & Gene Ans (red with diagonal stripes), and Acc=1 & GT Ans (yellow with diagonal stripes). For each domain, the first three bars (solid colors) represent the popularity of ground-truth entities (Pop_GT) for Llama3, Qwen2, and ChatGPT, respectively. The next three bars (striped) represent the popularity of generated entities (Pop_Ge) in incorrectly answered samples (Acc=0), with the striped blue, red, and yellow bars corresponding to Llama3, Qwen2, and ChatGPT, respectively. The final bar in each group (yellow with diagonal stripes) represents Pop_GT for correctly answered samples (Acc=1), which is also labeled as Pop_Ge in the caption. In all domains, the striped bars (incorrectly answered samples) are generally taller than the solid bars (correctly answered samples), indicating higher popularity of generated entities in wrong answers. The “Basketball” category shows the highest overall popularity values, with the striped red bar (Qwen2, Acc=0 & Gene Ans) reaching approximately 210. The “Movies” category shows the lowest values, with most bars under 60. The chart visually supports the textual claim that generated entities in incorrect answers tend to be more popular than ground-truth entities in correct answers.
